headline: Would have required sanctions on foreign people and groups who help the International Criminal Court pursue Americans or citizens of certain U.S. allies.
what_it_does: The bill would have required the President to block visas and freeze property of foreign individuals and entities that help the International Criminal Court (ICC) investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute protected persons. Protected persons would include Americans and people in the U.S., plus citizens or lawful residents of U.S. allies that have not joined the ICC treaty or accepted its authority. Sanctions would also have covered groups owned or controlled by those foreign persons, and their immediate family members would have been denied visas. The bill would also have canceled all U.S. funds set aside for the ICC and banned future funding for it.

who_it_affects.group: ICC officials, staff, and foreign people or companies who assist ICC cases
who_it_affects.how: They would have faced frozen U.S. property and blocked visas if they helped the ICC pursue a protected person.

who_it_affects.group: Immediate family members of sanctioned foreign persons
who_it_affects.how: They would have been blocked from getting U.S. visas.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. citizens, U.S. companies, and people in the United States
who_it_affects.how: They would have been named as protected persons, triggering sanctions on anyone who helps the ICC pursue them.

who_it_affects.group: Citizens and lawful residents of U.S. allies not part of the ICC
who_it_affects.how: They would also have been treated as protected persons under the bill.
It would have lost any U.S. government funding, with future funding banned.
